buildSteps.title: Decide the transformation
buildSteps.detail: Define exactly what the part must become — a flat sheet that folds into a box, a tube that widens inside a blood vessel — and how it should respond if it goes wrong.

buildSteps.title: Choose the trigger
buildSteps.detail: Pick the stimulus that will be available where the part is used: body heat, moisture, a light source or a magnetic field.

buildSteps.title: Formulate the ink or resin
buildSteps.detail: Blend a polymer with the right transition temperature or swelling behaviour, plus photo-initiators, crosslinkers or magnetic particles, and check it flows through a printhead.

buildSteps.title: Print with spatial control
buildSteps.detail: Deposit stiff and soft materials, and control fibre or channel direction, so that different regions strain by different amounts when activated.

buildSteps.title: Program the temporary shape
buildSteps.detail: For shape-memory polymers, heat above the transition temperature, deform the printed part into its stored shape and cool it under constraint so it holds.

buildSteps.title: Post-process
buildSteps.detail: Remove supports, fully cure or crosslink, and hydrate or pre-swell parts that will work in water or tissue.

buildSteps.title: Trigger and measure
buildSteps.detail: Apply the stimulus, record how fully and how fast the part reaches its target shape, and iterate on the design.

buildSteps.title: Integrate into a device
buildSteps.detail: Combine the actuator with its function — a stent with a drug coating, a deployable panel with a latch — and retest.

prerequisites.why: these supply the reversible change that 4D printing relies on; many are well characterised.
one object needs two or more materials placed precisely in three dimensions.
the concept was demonstrated around 2013 and has grown steadily, but remains mostly at laboratory scale.

prerequisites.tech: Predictive simulation of soft active structures
prerequisites.why: designs still rely heavily on trial and error because swelling and folding are hard to model.
implants need materials proven to be biocompatible and stable for years, not just for a demonstration.

pathway.milestone: laboratory demonstrations of self-folding sheets, swelling grippers and printed stents
pathway.unlocks: a catalogue of material behaviours and design rules.

pathway.milestone: medical devices in first human or clinical trials, such as implants that deploy at body temperature
pathway.unlocks: a demanding proving ground with clear safety and lifetime requirements.

pathway.milestone: deployable aerospace and industrial hardware that packs flat and expands on orbit or on site
pathway.unlocks: lower launch volume and fewer actuators and joints per part.

pathway.milestone: parts that sense and adapt repeatedly over their life, or self-repair
pathway.unlocks: machines and structures that reconfigure instead of being rebuilt.
